Junbin Cui1, Yong Wei1, Jianbo Wang1, Li Shang1 and Peng Lin2*   
Abstract 
In the power convergence network, a large number of intelligent power terminals 
(IPTs) are deployed, such as a variety of information collection terminals. Meanwhile, 
the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer dependable services for IPTs in environ-
ments with minimal or no infrastructure and then combine with the mobile edge 
computing to realize low-latency task services. In this article, we consider a problem 
of computation offloading and UAV trajectory design to minimize the task offload-
ing delay. Because the primal problem is non-convex, we first decompose it into two 
subproblems, i.e., joint computation offloading and resource allocation subproblem, 
and UAV trajectory design subproblem. For the first subproblem, we first reformulate 
it as a non-convex problem. And then, recognizing the problem’s high complexity, we 
choose to decompose it in a distributed form. Following this, leveraging the alternat-
ing direction method of multipliers, we introduce the joint computation offloading 
and resource allocation algorithm. For the second subproblem, we utilize the suc-
cessive convex approximation method to solve this non-convex problem. Utilizing 
the solutions obtained from these two subproblems, we have introduced the joint 
computation offloading and UAV trajectory design (JCOUTD) algorithm to tackle 
the primal problem. The simulation results reveal that in comparison with other bench-
mark methods, the proposed JCOUTD algorithm displays enhanced performance 
in reducing total task offloading delay.
Keywords:  UAV trajectory design, Power convergence network, Mobile edge 
computing (MEC), Alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), Successive 
convex approximation (SCA)
1  Introduction
The power convergence network is built on the foundation of an integrated, high-speed 
bidirectional communication network [1]. It achieves the goals of reliable, secure, cost-
effective, and safe grid through the applications of advanced sensing and measurement 
technology. In the power convergence network, a multitude of intelligent power termi-
nals (IPTs) are deployed, including temperature sensors, frequency sensors, and cam-
eras. These terminals generate numerous tasks that require computation processing [2]. 
In light of the limited computation capacity and energy resources available for IPTs, the

concept of mobile cloud computing (MCC) has been introduced. This approach involves 
offloading tasks to potent cloud centers, streamlining their processing. However, the 
large offloading delay is presented due to the long distance between the cloud center and 
the IPTs [3]. To address this challenge, the concept of mobile edge computing (MEC) has 
been introduced [4]. Thanks to the close proximity of MEC servers to IPTs, task offload-
ing delays can be significantly reduced.
Considering the environment and cost constraints, there is limited or no communica-
tion infrastructure in some rural areas. In this situation, the unmanned aerial vehicles 
(UAVs), known for their cost-effectiveness and exceptional mobility, have gained recog-
nition as an innovative solution for delivering dependable services to IPTs in environ-
ments with minimal or no infrastructure. Combining the UAVs and MEC can achieve the 
power convergence network goals of efficiency, intelligence, and reliability. Recently, the 
UAV-assisted computation offloading to minimize task offloading delay has been attract-
ing significant attention. Considering the UAVs flying delay, data transmission delay, 
and task computation delay, a joint UAV trajectory design and computation resource 
allocation problem were formulated to minimize the task offloading delay. In order to 
solve this problem, a machine learning framework based on the Q-learning algorithm 
was proposed [5]. To minimize system delay, a problem was formulated that involves 
dynamic UAVs functioning as relays and static UAVs serving as fixed base stations (BSs). 
This challenge encompasses joint task allocation and dynamic UAV trajectory design. 
To address it, the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm was employed 
[6]. Considering the software defined network can improve the quality of services for 
users, a problem was framed that involves joint task offloading and resource allocation 
to minimize task processing delay. Addressing the non-convex nature of this problem, a 
solution was introduced in the form of a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based algo-
rithm [7]. In order to make UVA more suitable for power convergence network, papers 
[8, 9] proposed the index modulation technology, which allowed certain terminals to be 
idle and utilized the different on-off states to transmit information or task offloading. In 
practical engineering, there are a large number of IPTs deployed in the power conver-
gence network. The complexity of the task offloading algorithm escalates significantly 
with the growth in the number of IPTs and UAVs. However, the complexity of the exist-
ing algorithms is very high, especially for the DRL algorithms. Therefore, it is essential 
to introduce a low-complexity distributed task offloading algorithm within the power 
convergence network.
Considering the shortcomings of existing literature, this paper proposes a joint com-
putation offloading and UAV trajectory design (JCOUTD) algorithm to minimize the 
task offloading delays within a power convergence network. The contributions of this 
paper mainly include the following aspects:
•	 We formulate a problem that addresses the joint computation offloading and UAV 
trajectory design. This problem is structured with the objective of minimizing the 
total task offloading delay for IPTs, all the while taking into account factors such as 
task offloading delay, IPTs’ energy consumption, and system resource constraints.
•	 Considering the coupling of optimization variables and the non-convexity of the 
formulated problem, the primal problem is decomposed into two subproblems. By

The structure of this paper is as follows: In Sect. 2, we provide an overview of related 
works. Section 3 introduces the methods in this paper. Section 4 introduces the system 
model, encompassing the network model, communication model, and computation 
model. In Sect. 5, we outline the problem of minimizing task offloading delay, breaking 
it down into two subproblems. Section 6 introduces the joint computation offloading 
and resource allocation (JCORA) algorithm for resolving the joint computation off-
loading and resource allocation subproblem. The UAV trajectory design subproblem is 
addressed using the SCA method in Sect. 7. In Sect. 8, we propose the JCOUTD algo-
rithm, building upon the solutions from the two subproblems. To validate the effective-
ness of the proposed algorithms, Sect.  9 presents simulation results and discussion. 
Finally, in Section 10, we draw our conclusions.
2  Related works
Resource allocation and UAV trajectory design have recently garnered significant atten-
tion. These endeavors can be categorized into three groups based on their different 
objectives.
The primary objective is to minimize energy consumption. Considering the fairness 
of the UAVs, a 3D multi-UAV trajectory design was formulated to reduce system energy 
consumption, where users select target UAVs for task computing. Utilizing the multi-
agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) method, an optimal solution 
was successfully obtained [10]. A system energy consumption minimization problem 
was studied by jointly optimizing the beamforming vectors of UAVs, the computa-
tion resources of UAVs, the UAVs trajectory, and the transmission power of users. In 
order to solve the non-convex problem, a three stage iterative algorithm was proposed 
[11]. In order to extend the UAVs operating time, Wang et  al. investigated the prob-
lem to minimize the energy consumption of UAVs. By decomposing the problem into 
two subproblems, an iterative algorithm was proposed to obtain the optimal solution 
[12]. Considering the high maneuverability of UAVs can enhance the communication 
and computation performance, a joint resource allocation, user association, and power 
control algorithm was proposed by utilizing the centralized multi-agent reinforcement 
learning method [13]. Du et al. formulated a problem of minimizing the UAV energy 
consumption by jointly optimizing the users association, computation resource allo-
cation, UAV hovering time, and wireless powering duration time. By transforming the 
problem into a convex problem and applying the flow-shop scheduling techniques, an 
alternative algorithm was proposed [14].
The second objective is to enhance computational efficiency. To maintain the sta-
bility of the dynamic task data queue and minimize secure computation require-
ments, a problem was formulated involving binary offloading decisions and resource 
allocation to maximize the computation efficiency. Through the application of the

Dinkelbach method to render the problem more tractable, a novel online edge learn-
ing offloading algorithm was developed [15]. Considering the UAV-assisted relaying 
in the MEC networks, a computation efficiency maximization problem was formu-
lated by jointly optimizing the UAV trajectory, computation, and radio resources. By 
utilizing the Dinkelbach method, the block coordinate descent (BCD) method and 
the SCA technique, an algorithm was proposed [16]. Considering the limited system 
resources, finite UAV energy, and interference between the uplink and downlink, 
a joint computation allocation, UAV trajectory design, and radio resource alloca-
tion problem was formulated to maximize the computation efficiency. After that, 
a multi-stage alternative optimization algorithm was proposed [17]. Taking into 
account the potential for Internet of Things (IoT) nodes to utilize energy harvested 
from the UAV’s radio frequency, two optimization problems focusing on maximiz-
ing computation bits were framed, considering both partial and binary offloading 
scenarios. To tackle these issues, two iterative algorithms were devised for solving 
these different problems [18]. To optimize users’ computation bits while adhering 
to fairness constraints, a novel algorithm called soft actor-critic (SAC)-based UAV 
trajectory planning and resource allocation (SAC-TR) was introduced [19].
The third objective centers on minimizing task offloading delays. Zhang et al. har-
nessed the UAV’s dual roles as a computation node and relay node to devise a prob-
lem aimed at minimizing average user latency. To tackle this challenge, the problem 
was decomposed into three subproblems, and an approximation algorithm was pro-
posed for its resolution [20]. In order to meet the requirements of mobile broadband 
communication (eMBB) and massive machine-type communication (mMTC) users, 
an optimization problem to minimize the task offloading delay was formulated. And 
then, the authors proposed the Rosen’s gradient projection algorithm to solve this 
problem [21]. Han et al. introduced a problem aimed at minimizing the average task 
offloading delay by jointly optimizing user association and UAV deployment. By uti-
lizing the optimal transport theory and classical particle swarm optimization algo-
rithm, the problem was solved [22]. Hu et al. devised a problem with the objective 
of minimizing the maximum delay, achieved by jointly optimizing computation off-
loading, computation resource allocation, and UAV trajectory. To address this chal-
lenge, the authors introduced a novel penalty dual decomposition-based algorithm 
[23]. To minimize task offloading delay, a problem involving the joint optimization 
of UAV placement, resource allocation, and computation offloading was formulated. 
An algorithm utilizing the double deep Q-Learning (DDQN) and deep deterministic 
policy gradient (DDPG) algorithms was introduced to obtain a near-optimal solu-
tion [24].
In practical engineering, there are a large number of IPTs deployed in the power 
convergence network. As the number of IPTs and UAVs increases, the complexity of 
the task offloading algorithm will escalate significantly, especially for the centralized 
algorithms and DRL algorithms in the existing works. Therefore, taking into account 
practical considerations, it is essential to develop a distributed task offloading algo-
rithm with low complexity for the power convergence network.

3  Methods/experimental
The objective of this study is to reduce task offloading delays within a power conver-
gence network through the joint optimization of resource allocation and UAV trajec-
tory design. Given that the problem is non-convex, it is necessary to break it down into 
two subproblems: one addressing joint computation offloading and resource allocation 
and the other tackling UAV trajectory design. For the first subproblem, we first utilize 
variable relaxation and variable substitution to reformulate it as a non-convex problem. 
And then, the problem is approached in a distributed manner using the ADMM method. 
This leads to the introduction of the JCORA algorithm based on the derived solution. 
Meanwhile, for the second subproblem, the non-convex issue is addressed using the 
SCA method. According to the solutions of two subproblems, we propose the JCOUTD 
algorithm. In addition, Matlab simulation results substantiate the effectiveness of the 
JCOUTD algorithm as proposed.

allocation, computation resource allocation, and UAV trajectory design to minimize 
the task offloading delay. As this problem constitutes a non-convex optimization

9  Simulation results and discussion
In this section, we assess the effectiveness of the proposed JCOUTD algorithm 
through numerical simulations. The system comprises one BS equipped with a MEC 
server and three UAVs. Each UAV serves five IPTs, and the bandwidth of each UAV is 
5 MHz. The transmission power of each IPT is 0.01 W, the maximal CPU-cycle fre-
quency is 40 MHz, and the conversion coefficient is 10−27 . The MEC server’s maximal 
CPU-cycle frequency is 1 GHz, and the transmission rate from the UAV to the BS 
is 10 Mbits. Task sizes and computation resource requirements follow Gaussian dis-
tributions with skn ∼N(300, 10) and ckn ∼N(10, 0.1) , respectively. Data size is meas-
ured in KB, and computation resources are measured in Megacycles. The maximum 
delay tolerance is 0.3 s. The UAV operates at an altitude of 20 m with a maximum 
speed of 20 m/s. Each period has a duration of 10 s, and each time slot lasts for 0.5 s.
To assess the performance of the proposed JCOUTD algorithm, we conduct com-
parisons with the following three algorithms.

•	 Penalty block coordinate descent (P-BCD) algorithm: In this algorithm, the primal 
problem is decomposed into four subproblems, which are solved alternately and iter-
atively [35].
Figure 2 depicts the relationship between the total task offloading delay and band-
width under various algorithms. In the case of the ASLC algorithm, the total task off-
loading delay remains constant as it is independent of bandwidth. Conversely, for the 
other algorithms, as bandwidth increases, each task can be allocated more bandwidth, 
resulting in a reduction in task transmission time. In comparison with the P-BCD 
algorithm, when the bandwidth increases from 5 to 5.5 MHz, the JCOUTD algorithm 
shows a reduction of approximately 3.47% in the total task offloading delay.
Figure  3 depicts the relationship between the total task offloading delay and 
the computation resources of the MEC server for different algorithms. In the case 
of the ASLC algorithm, the task offloading delay remains constant as the computa-
tion resources of the MEC server increase. This consistency arises because all tasks 
are locally processed by the IPTs, rendering the task offloading delay independent 
of the MEC server’s computation resources. In contrast, for the other algorithms, 
the total task offloading delay decreases as the computation resources of the MEC 
server increase. This decline is attributed to the increased availability of computa-
tion resources that can be allocated to each task. When compared to the P-BCD algo-
rithm, a growth in the computation resources of the MEC server from 1 GHz to 1.5 
GHz results in the JCOUTD algorithm achieving a reduction of approximately 3.15% 
in the total task offloading delay.

10  Conclusions
In this paper, we introduced a problem of joint computation offloading and UAV 
trajectory design with the objective of minimizing task offloading delay. Due to the 
problem’s non-convex nature, we divided it into two subproblems and resolved them 
using the ADMM and SCA methods. Building on the solutions to these subproblems, 
we put forward the JCOUTD algorithm. The simulation results confirm the efficacy of 
the JCOUTD algorithm proposed in this paper.

Abstract: In the power convergence network, a large number of intelligent power terminals (IPTs) are deployed, such as a variety of information collection terminals. Meanwhile, the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer dependable services for IPTs in environ- ments with minimal or no infrastructure and then combine with the mobile edge computing to realize low-latency task services. In this article, we consider a problem of computation offloading and UAV trajectory design to minimize the task offload- ing delay. Because the primal problem is non-convex, we first decompose it into two subproblems, i.e., joint computation offloading and resource allocation subproblem, and UAV trajectory design subproblem. For the first subproblem, we first reformulate it as a non-convex problem. And then, recognizing the problem’s high complexity, we choose to decompose it in a distributed form. Following this, leveraging the alternat- ing direction method of multipliers, we introduce the joint computation offloading and resource allocation algorithm. For the second subproblem, we utilize the suc- cessive convex approximation method to solve this non-convex problem. Utilizing the solutions obtained from these two subproblems, we have introduced the joint computation offloading and UAV trajectory design (JCOUTD) algorithm to tackle the primal problem. The simulation results reveal that in comparison with other bench- mark methods, the proposed JCOUTD algorithm displays enhanced performance in reducing total task offloading delay.
